battle.name: 唐末農民戰爭
battle.brief: 乾符二年（875）正月河南水旱饑荒，夏秋間王仙芝、黃巢先後在曹、濮起兵，轉戰江南、嶺南；廣明元年（880）十二月大軍入長安建齊，僖宗奔蜀；中和三年（883）李克用率沙陀騎兵入關，義軍退出長安，884年首領死於泰山狼虎谷。卡面斯巴達長矛屬方陣步卒，唐軍的槊才是當時的長柄兵器。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 交戰的一方是唐王朝的中央朝廷與各道藩鎮聯軍，另一方是河南饑民與鹽梟為骨幹、由王仙芝與黃巢先後率領的起義軍。唐僖宗李儇即位時，天下分為數十道，軍政財權由節度使分割，禁軍與神策軍歸宦官田令孜掌握，京師宿衛與各地鎮軍互不隸屬。河南道是唐廷的糧倉與漕運樞紐，汴州、洛陽兩處的倉儲與漕船積了一個王朝的餘糧，因此成了叛軍與官軍爭奪的第一個目標。起義軍方面並無正式編制：乾符元年（874）河南先水後旱，饑民結隊而行；乾符二年（875）曹州鹽商王仙芝聚眾數千，曹州冤句的鹽梟黃巢與之互為犄角；攻城之後收攏降卒、散卒與亡命，眾數由數千增至十餘萬，其後合為一軍，兵權歸黃巢獨握。官軍方面，先由兗鄆節度使張軍陀、宣武軍節度使王忠嗣、淮西軍節度使王仲甫、昭義軍節度使孟方立分道討伐，彼此不肯併力；僖宗一面下詔招撫，一面借外力，命河東沙陀節度使李克用與宣武軍節度使朱溫引兵勤王。於是這場戰爭的指揮系統，一端是無法編成的流民軍團，另一端是互不信任的諸鎮聯軍，中間夾著一支漸漸私兵化的禁軍。
countriesEn: Two sides fought this war: the central court of the Tang dynasty together with the armies of the regional governors, and the rebel host that grew out of the famine victims of Henan under the leadership first of Wang Xianzhi and then of Huang Chao. When Emperor Xizong, Li Xuan, took the throne the empire was divided into dozens of circuits, with military, political and fiscal power carved up by the jiedushi; the imperial guards and the Divine Strategy Army were in the hands of the eunuch Tian Lingzi, and the garrison of the capital stood in no relation to the armies of the circuits. Henan Circuit was the granary of the court and the pivot of the canal transport, and the depots of Bian prefecture and of the eastern capital Luoyang held the surplus grain of a whole dynasty, which is why they became the first prizes contested between the rebels and the government troops. The insurgents had no formal establishment at all. After the flood and then the drought that struck Henan in 874, famine victims banded together; in 875 the salt merchant Wang Xianzhi of Cao prefecture gathered several thousand men, and Huang Chao, a smuggler of Yuanju in Caozhou, led a band of the same trade in his own right. After taking towns the rebels absorbed surrendered soldiers, scattered men and runaways, their numbers rose from several thousands to over a hundred thousand, and the bands later merged into a single army under Huang Chao's sole command. The Tang side opened with separate columns led by Zhang Juntao of Yanzhou-Yong, Wang Zhongsi of Xuanwu, Wang Zhongfu of Huaixi and Meng Fangli of Zhaoyi, none of whom would cooperate with the others. Xizong at once issued edicts of pardon and summoned outside help, ordering the Shatuo jiedushi Li Keyong of Hedong and the Xuanwu jiedushi Zhu Wen to bring troops to the capital. The command structure of this war therefore had at one end a militia of refugees that could never be organised, and at the other a league of circuits that did not trust one another, with a guard army that was itself turning private lying between them.
people: 王仙芝是這場戰爭的第一位首領。他是河南道曹州人，出身鹽商，熟悉鄉里道路、鹽價與漕運行情，通曉騎射而好談兵事；乾符二年（875）河南饑荒，他散財聚眾，起兵於曹、濮之間，連破州縣、殺官吏、掠倉場，眾數由數千增至十餘萬，一度進逼汴洛。乾符四年（877）他在羊馬城與陶家川一線被張軍陀追敗，轉戰千里；乾符五年（878）七月在攻圍潞州時病歿軍中，被部將尚復乘譁變所殺，首級送與黃巢。黃巢是曹州冤句人，世代以鹽為業，本是浙西的私鹽梟；他自號「沖天香陣」，聞仙芝起兵便遣其弟率眾來會，兩軍並立而不相統屬，仙芝死後才合為一軍，全軍推黃巢為帥，眾至數十萬，號令嚴整，攻城掠地之後常能以重賞收編降卒與潰散鄉勇。他留下的「待到秋來九月八，我花開後百花殺」等詩句，後世遂以「黃巢」與「黃巢之亂」指稱這場動亂。核心人物還包括尚讓、查莊、畢師鐸等部將，以及叛出唐廷的宣武軍節度使朱溫——他以討黃巢為名收編叛軍，後來反噬唐室。官軍方面，除張軍陀、王忠嗣、王仲甫、孟方立等宿將之外，真正扭轉戰局的是河東沙陀節度使李克用，他率本部騎兵南下，於中和三年（883）大破黃巢於長安附近，迫使義軍退出關中。僖宗李儇在亂中倚重宦官田令孜，數次出奔，884年返回長安時，禁軍與神策軍已裂為數部，各擁其主。
peopleEn: Wang Xianzhi was the first leader of this war. He was a native of Cao prefecture in Henan Circuit, born into a family of salt merchants, familiar with the roads, the salt prices and the grain traffic of his home district, at home on horseback and with the bow, and given to talking of warfare. When famine broke over Henan in 875 he scattered his money to gather the hungry and rose in the country between Cao and Pu, taking prefecture after prefecture, killing officials and emptying the granaries; his numbers grew from several thousands to more than a hundred thousand and at one point came close to Bian and Luo. In 877 he was beaten and chased back along the Yangma and Taojia lines by Zhang Juntao, and he wheeled across a thousand li; in the seventh month of 878, while besieging Lu prefecture, he fell gravely ill and was killed in a mutiny by his own commander Shang Fu, who cut off his head and carried it to Huang Chao. Huang Chao was a native of Yuanju in Caozhou, whose family had lived on salt for generations and who had been a smuggler of the western Zhejiang coast. He called himself the army of the fragrant standard that pierces the sky, and when he heard that Xianzhi had risen he sent his younger brother with troops to join him; the two forces stood side by side without subordination, and only after Xianzhi's death did they merge into one army, with Huang Chao raised to sole command over a host numbered in tens of thousands, strict in discipline, and skilled at buying over surrendered soldiers and scattered local bands with prompt rewards after each town it took. His lines beginning with the coming of the ninth month of autumn, when his flowers will bloom and all other flowers are killed, are why later generations speak of the disturbance by the name of Huang Chao. Among the other central figures were the commanders Shang Rang, Zha Zhuang and Bi Shiduo, and above all Zhu Wen, jiedushi of Xuanwu, who had himself defected from the Tang court, took over rebel troops under the banner of fighting Huang Chao, and later turned against the dynasty. On the Tang side, besides such regulars as Zhang Juntao, Wang Zhongsi, Wang Zhongfu and Meng Fangli, the man who truly turned the war was Li Keyong, the Shatuo jiedushi of Hedong, who led his cavalry south and crushed Huang Chao near the capital in 883, forcing the insurgents out of Guanzhong. Xizong, Li Xuan, relied throughout the disorder on the eunuch Tian Lingzi and fled the capital more than once; when he came back to Chang'an in 884 the imperial guards and the Divine Strategy Army had already split into several factions, each following its own chief.
kits: 卡面這件斯巴達長矛是古希臘重裝步兵方陣所用的長柄矛，約兩米長，槍身多取白楊等輕木，矛頭為青銅，槍尾留有銅套，可插地支撐、可用以格擋並在盾後換手；方陣密集排列時矛尖一律朝前，左翼重裝兵以圓盾護身，最前列的槍兵要撐住接戰的第一擊。這種武器從未在中國出現，與它最接近的中國兵器是矛與槊，以及矛、盾並用的「矛盾」之制；唐人李筌所撰《太白陰經》列舉唐代兵仗，即以槊、矛、盾、弩、甲為大宗，其中槊長約二米，與斯巴達長矛相仿，出兵時與長刀、橫刀、陌刀同列，是藩鎮步卒與禁軍常用的長柄兵器。近世學者有以唐代「矛盾」合用比擬希臘長矛配小盾者，但兩者形制與戰法未必盡同，此說至今仍有爭議。晚唐的實際裝備另有其貌：官軍步卒著明光鎧、札甲，佩長刀與橫刀，用角弓弩、擘張弩與連弩；弩機按石分等，擘張弩需二人張弦，有效射程在二百至三百步之間，連弩架於城垛射孔之後，以射速壓制攀城者。攻城一方備有雲梯、飛雲梯、撞竿、投石機所發的石彈、火球與猛火油，敦煌出土的唐人兵書殘卷與弩具清冊中亦見槊與角弓弩的記載。義軍則大量把鋤、鐮、斧、竹竿改造成槍械，皮甲布甲雜用，缺鎧者多；其騎兵比例甚高，多用驃馬，與唐廷倚重的沙陀騎兵正相對。卡面這件希臘長矛的意義在於，它把方陣步卒「以長兵定站位」的基本道理擺在牌面上——這正是晚唐軍隊在城牆與野地之間反覆實踐的課題。
kitsEn: The Spartan spear on the card face is the long pike of the Greek heavy infantry phalanx, about two metres long, its shaft usually of light wood such as poplar, its head of bronze, with a bronze cap at the butt that could be planted in the ground, used to parry, and allowed the weapon to be changed hands behind the shield. In a tightly packed phalanx the points faced forward in one line, the heavy troops on the left flank were covered by their round shields, and the front rank of pikemen had to hold the first shock of contact. This weapon never existed in China, and the Chinese arms closest to it are the spear and the mao, together with the pairing of spear and shield known as the dun mao. Li Quan of the Tang, in his military treatise Taibai Yinjing, lists the arms of the dynasty, and the mao, the spear, the shield, the crossbow and the armour make up the greater part of that list; the mao was about two metres long, close to the length of the Spartan pike, and went into the field alongside the long sabre, the single-edged sabre and the heavy dao, and was standard equipment in the foot of the circuits' armies and of the imperial guard. Modern scholars have proposed comparing the Tang pairing of spear and shield with the Greek long spear and small shield, but the forms and the fighting methods are not necessarily the same, and the point remains disputed. The actual equipment of the late Tang looked different again: government infantry wore bright plate and lamellar armour, carried the long sabre and the single-edged sabre, and used the horn bow crossbow, the heavy-drawn crossbow and the repeating crossbow. Crossbows were graded by stone, one stone being about one hundred and twenty catties; the heavy crossbow needed two men to draw it and had an effective range of two hundred to three hundred paces, while the repeating crossbow was set up behind the arrow slits of the ramparts to crush men climbing the wall with the weight of its rate of fire. The besieging side brought scaling ladders, flying ladders, battering poles, the stone shot of the catapults, fire balls and fire oil; Tang military manuscripts and lists of crossbow equipment recovered at Dunhuang also record the mao and the horn bow crossbow. The insurgents made weapons out of hoes, sickles, axes and bamboo poles, wore a mixture of leather and cloth armour, and many had no armour at all. Their proportion of cavalry was very high and they rode mostly strong piebald war horses, and they faced the Shatuo cavalry on whom the Tang court came to rely. The point of the Greek spear on the card is that it sets out on the face of the card the basic principle of the phalanx foot, that the position of the line is settled by the long weapons, which was precisely the problem the late Tang armies worked at again and again between wall and field.
tactics: 起義軍的戰術核心是不戍守、不列陣的流動戰。起義初期隊伍輕裝自持，日間偃旗息鼓、鼓噪擾敵，入夜銜枚疾行，天明之前撲向州縣城門；得手即縱兵搜括倉廩、驅畜而去，不作久屯，使官軍雖有城池卻難以確定敵蹤。攻城手段依城而異：地勢平緩者用雲梯、飛雲梯逼近，倉場與城門密集處用火攻，火器遇雨則轉為穴地掘進與決水灌城；史傳有義軍攻潼關、華州用火器與穴地之記載，具體細節諸說並存。攻不下便轉掠他處，這條規矩使起義軍的兵力與糧秣始終流動，卻也意味著它始終沒有攻下洛陽、汴州兩座巨城。黃巢入關時的部署也依此原則：前鋒分兵兩路，一路由尚讓、李思敬趨潼關，一路自王重榮處假道河中，試圖迂迴關中；因河中與昭義兩鎮拒絕配合而受挫，潼關在援軍到之前被攻破。官軍的戰術則以據城死守為主：節度使各守封疆，寧可坐失戰機也不肯併兵，諸道勤王軍雖集於京師卻互不隸屬，結果在洛陽、陝州一線被各個擊破。883年後戰局改變：沙陀騎兵以夜襲與高速機動馳援關中，於梁田陂一線大敗巢軍，義軍放火焚燒宮室而走，退保藍田、陳州、泰山一線；此時雙方都明白，決定勝負的不再是城牆與投石，而是騎兵的速度與糧道。糧秣方面，義軍靠就地徵發與掠倉，官軍靠汴河、廣通渠運江淮之粟，一旦失河南，京師軍食便只能仰給江淮，運轉遲緩成為致命弱點。
tacticsEn: The core of the insurgents' method was a war of movement that neither garrisoned nor formed up. In the first months the columns travelled light, kept their flags furled and beat drums by day to make noise and unsettle the enemy, moved at night with their mouths plugged, and fell on the gates of the prefectures and counties before dawn. On success they swept the granaries, drove off the livestock and left again without making a long camp, so that the Tang army, though it owned the walls, could hardly track them down. The means of assault varied with the place: where the ground was gentle they brought scaling ladders and flying ladders close to the wall, where the storehouses and the gates were crowded they used fire, and when the fire weapons failed in the rain they turned to tunnelling and to breaching the ditch with water. The histories do record the insurgents using fire weapons and tunnels against Tong Pass and Huazhou, though the details are given in several conflicting ways. When a city did not fall they moved on and plundered elsewhere; that rule kept the strength and the supplies of the rebel army in constant motion, but it also meant they never took either of the two great cities of Luoyang and Bian. Huang Chao's deployment when he entered Guanzhong followed the same principle: the advance was split into two columns, one under Shang Rang and Li Sijing pressing on Tong Pass, the other seeking a route through Hedong by way of Wang Chongrong, in order to turn the pass from the flank; it was frustrated because the circuits of Hedong and Zhaoyi refused to cooperate, and Tong Pass fell before help could arrive. The Tang tactics were to hold the walled city and fight to the death. Each jiedushi guarded his own borders and would rather lose an opportunity than commit troops to a neighbour; the armies summoned from the circuits to the capital mustered there without any subordination to one another, and were defeated in detail along the line of Luoyang and Shaozhou. After 883 the situation changed: the Shatuo cavalry came to the relief of Guanzhong by night raid and by high-speed manoeuvre, beat the army of Chao in a line near Liangtian, and the insurgents set fire to the palaces and withdrew, falling back on Lantian, Chenzhou and Taishan. From that point both sides understood that what decided the war was no longer the wall and the catapult but the speed of cavalry and the grain road. On supplies the insurgents depended on levies taken on the spot and on plundered depots, while the Tang drew on the grain of the Jiang and Huai regions carried by the Bian River and the Guangqu canal; once Henan was lost, the military food of the capital could be supplied only from the southeast, and the slowness of that haul became a fatal weakness.
data: 可核的數字並不多，各史記載互有出入，這裡只列比較可靠與明確存疑者。時間上，一般把這場動亂定在乾符元年（874）河南災荒至中和四年（884）黃巢死於泰山之間，前後約十年；王仙芝自乾符二年（875）起兵至乾符五年（878）病歿，單獨領導約三年，其後由黃巢收拾舊部再戰六年。兵眾數量：起義初期「聚眾數千」諸說較為可信，兩年後已增至十餘萬；黃巢軍後來號稱百萬，實際當在數十萬之譜，《舊唐書》等所記「眾至百萬」應視為誇大。官軍方面，唐末禁軍額數諸說從十餘萬至二十萬不等，至乾符年間逃亡過半，朝廷只能以客軍與募兵補缺，故各節度使所部往往自成一軍。883年李克用率沙陀眾及北方諸部兵南下，諸書記數萬至五萬不等，數萬騎為公認；同年十月，巢軍退出長安。距離上，曹州至長安逾一千三百里，義軍自河南轉戰江南、閩、嶺南再折返關中，行程數千里而糧秣不給，絕大多數靠就地徵發。器械方面，唐弩以石分等，一石約合今一百二十斤，擘張弩需二人張弦，有效射程二百至三百步；槊長約二米；投石機所發石彈諸書記重數十斤，射程數百步；雲梯高十餘丈。雙方總傷亡數現存史籍無可靠統計，陣亡與被俘人數多不可考。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked are few and the records disagree with one another, so only the better supported figures and the openly doubtful ones are set out here. On timing, the disturbance is generally placed between the famine that struck Henan in 874 and the death of Huang Chao at Taishan in 884, a span of about ten years. Wang Xianzhi led from his rising in 875 to his death in 878, some three years on his own, and Huang Chao then gathered up the old forces and fought for six years more. On numbers: the phrase that the rising began with several thousands is the more credible, and within two years the force had grown to more than a hundred thousand; the rebel host was later said to number a million, but the real figure was in the tens of thousands, and the statement in the Jiu Tangshu that there were a million men should be read as an exaggeration. On the government side, the strength of the imperial guard is given in the late Tang at anywhere from a hundred thousand to two hundred thousand, but by the Qianfu years more than half had deserted, the court could fill the ranks only with mercenaries and recruited men, and the troops of each jiedushi therefore tended to form a private army of their own. In 883 Li Keyong led the Shatuo and the tribes of the north southward; the histories give from several thousand to fifty thousand, and a number in the thousands of horsemen is accepted. In the same year, in the tenth month, the army of Chao withdrew from Chang'an. On distances, Cao prefecture and Chang'an are more than thirteen hundred li apart, and the insurgents wheeled from Henan through Jiangnan, Min and Lingnan before turning back into Guanzhong, a march of thousands of li without supply, the greater part of it fed by levies taken on the spot. On weapons, Tang crossbows were graded by stone, one stone being about one hundred and twenty catties; the heavy crossbow needed two men to draw it and had an effective range of two hundred to three hundred paces; the mao was about two metres long; the stone shot of the catapults is recorded by the histories as weighing several tens of catties with a range of several hundred paces; and the scaling ladders stood more than ten zhang high. For total casualties on either side the surviving histories hold no reliable statistics, and the numbers killed and captured are largely unknown.
cause: 這場戰爭的起因是多重壓力同時作用在河南道。土地一端，均田制早已崩壞，官僚與寺觀兼併莊園，兩稅法按資產而非按戶等征收，逃亡與隱匿戶口成為常態，小民既失田產又無官糧可依；商業一端，榷鹽專賣把鹽價壓到私販無利可圖或無路可走的境地，鹽梟群體由此坐大，王仙芝、黃巢皆是其中的能者；天災一端，乾符元年（874）河南先大水繼以大旱，飛蝗遍起，漕渠淤塞，漕運斷絕，京師與河南的倉儲同時吃緊。政治一端，自懿宗以來藩鎮割據，兵為將有、財為將有，中央對河南各鎮只剩節度使的任命權；僖宗李儇怠於朝政，好擊球、鬥雞、與伶人飲宴，把榷鹽與軍需一併交給宦官田令孜，加派苛急，軍欠餉而逃亡者眾。於是乾符二年（875）正月起，饑民成群結隊流入州縣，盜劫、掠倉、殺吏的事層出不窮；王仙芝散財為饑民聚集人望，黃巢以鹽幫為骨幹，兩人先後起兵，而朝廷的處置不是賑災而是防範：既無常平倉與義倉可放，又怕地方擅出官粟，只好以招撫與賞格嘗試用金帛買回秩序，結果招撫與討伐交替，叛軍在兩者之間越戰越強。
causeEn: The outbreak of this war came from several pressures bearing on Henan Circuit at the same time. On land, the equal-field system had long since collapsed, officialdom and the monasteries had absorbed the estates, the two-tax law assessed wealth rather than households, flight and concealment of households had become normal, and the small folk had neither fields nor any prospect of official grain. In trade, the salt monopoly drove the salt price to a point where smuggling was either unprofitable or impossible, and the smuggling bands grew accordingly; Wang Xianzhi and Huang Chao were among the most capable of them. On weather, Henan was struck in 874 by a great flood followed by a great drought, locusts swarmed, the canal silted up and the grain traffic was cut, so that the depots of the capital and of Henan were strained at the same time. In politics, since the reign of Emperor Yizong the circuits had become independent principalities, troops and revenue belonged to the generals, and the centre retained over the circuits of Henan little more than the right of appointing the jiedushi. Xizong, Li Xuan, was negligent in state affairs, fond of ball games, cockfighting and drinking with entertainers, and handed the salt monopoly and the military supply to the eunuch Tian Lingzi; the surtaxes were harsh, the army went unpaid, and desertions multiplied. From the first month of 875 the famine victims poured into the prefectures and counties in bands, and robbery, the emptying of granaries and the killing of officials followed one another. Wang Xianzhi scattered his money and gathered renown among the hungry, Huang Chao used the smuggling bands as his skeleton, and the two rose in turn. The court's answer was not relief but containment: with neither the ever-normal granaries nor the charitable granaries able to release enough grain, and with fear that the localities would give out store grain on their own initiative, the only instrument left was pacification and reward, an attempt to buy the peace back with money and silk. The result was that pacification and attack alternated, and the rebels grew stronger in the gap between the two.
impact: 唐末農民戰爭對唐室的傷害，與其說是一場戰敗，不如說是一次國家結構的拆解。第一，長安與洛陽兩京相繼失守，僖宗自洛陽出奔華州、幸蜀，884年才得以還都；皇帝出奔在唐末成為常態，流亡朝廷與河北、河東藩鎮之間的關係由此定型，中央號令出不了京畿。第二，討平動亂的過程把全國的兵權推向地方：朱溫以宣武軍節度使收編黃巢降眾，擊敗秦宗權之後盡有汴宋之地；李克用以河東節度使鎮守河東，與朱溫自此爭衡河北；李茂貞據鳳翔，各鎮自募兵、自徵稅、自置將，朝廷無力過問。第三，戰亂把河南道與關中的兩處核心稅源與漕源同時摧毀，唐廷此後只能倚重江淮、兩浙與嶺南的財賦，江南第一次因為戰亂的推移而獲得大規模開發的契機，江西由邊地一躍成為重要的賦稅與漕運之區；同時大批流民被裹入軍伍，脫產為兵成為亂軍壯大的主要方式，也使亂軍的兵源在地理上由河南向江淮、嶺南擴散。第四，技術層面也有變化：火藥與猛火油在攻城中的使用更頻繁，藩鎮騎兵代替京師禁軍成為野戰主力，兵器與戰法的更新不再由朝廷主導，而由各鎮自行決定。後世史家所謂這場動亂「間接造成唐朝滅亡」，指的正是這一連串的連鎖反應。
impactEn: The damage this war did to the Tang was less a defeat than the taking apart of the structure of the state. First, the two capitals of Chang'an and Luoyang fell in turn, and Xizong fled from Luoyang to Huazhou and then to Shu, returning to the capital only in 884; flight of the emperor became a normal feature of the late Tang, and the relation between the government in exile and the circuits of Hebei and Hedong was fixed for good, with the orders of the centre never reaching beyond the capital district. Second, the process of suppressing the revolt pushed the military power of the empire into the hands of the localities. Zhu Wen, jiedushi of Xuanwu, took over the surrendered followers of Huang Chao and, after beating Qin Zongquan, held the whole of Bian and Song; Li Keyong, jiedushi of Hedong, held Bin and Fen, and from that time competed with Zhu Wen for the north; Li Maozhen held Fengxiang; each circuit recruited its own soldiers, levied its own taxes and appointed its own generals, and the court could do nothing. Third, the war destroyed at once the two principal sources of tax and of canal transport in Henan and Guanzhong, and the Tang court had to lean from then on on the wealth of the Jiang and Huai regions, of the two Zhe and of Lingnan. Jiangnan received for the first time the opening that the shock of the fighting gave it, and Jiangxi rose from a frontier region to a major source of tribute and of grain transport. At the same time large numbers of displaced people were taken into the armies, so that leaving the fields to bear arms became the principal way in which the rebel host grew, and the source of its recruits spread geographically from Henan towards the southeast. Fourth, there were changes of a technical kind: gunpowder and fire oil were used more often in assaults on walls, the cavalry of the circuits rather than the imperial guard became the main force in the field, and the renewal of weapons and of fighting methods was no longer led by the court but decided by each circuit for itself. What later historians meant when they said that this disturbance indirectly brought about the fall of the Tang is precisely this chain of consequences.
result: 結局並不是任何一方的徹底勝利。中和四年（884），黃巢在泰山狼虎谷一帶被唐軍追及，走投無路而死，其部眾或散或降：尚讓以郢州降唐，朝廷照例授以官爵；其餘隊伍被朱溫、李克用與後來盤踞蔡州的秦宗權各收一部，叛軍的武裝從此化為藩鎮的私兵。官軍收復長安與洛陽，僖宗於同年返回京師，表面上的秩序似乎恢復，但實際上這場戰爭留下的結果是：朝廷平叛的兵源被自己人瓜分，河北、河東、關中的藩鎮以「討亂」的名義取得兵權與地盤，秦宗權以蔡州節度使坐大、自稱帝號，至888年被朱溫與李克用合軍打敗身死，動亂的餘波又延續了近十年。就全局看，這場戰爭以叛軍首領全滅、官軍士氣耗盡、藩鎮坐大而收場：唐廷在河南與關中再也組織不出一支能服從中央的部隊，而以朱溫、李克用為首的藩鎮在收拾完亂局之後彼此攻伐，把唐室的最後一點權力也消耗殆盡。907年朱溫迫僖宗禪位，唐朝滅亡，與這場戰爭所打碎的財政、兵制與權力結構直接相連。
resultEn: The outcome was not a complete victory for either side. In 884, at the valley of Langhu below Taishan, Huang Chao was run down by the Tang troops, cornered and killed; his followers were scattered or surrendered. Shang Rang came over to the Tang with the prefecture of Ying and was granted an office in the customary way; the rest of the host was divided up in part by Zhu Wen, in part by Li Keyong, and in part by Qin Zongquan, who later held the circuit of Cai, so that the armed force of the revolt turned into the private armies of the circuits. The government recovered Chang'an and Luoyang, and Xizong returned to the capital in the same year, so that order seemed to be restored on the surface. What this war really left behind was different: the manpower with which the court suppressed the revolt was divided up by its own people; the circuits of Hebei, Hedong and Guanzhong obtained troops and territory in the name of stamping out disorder; Qin Zongquan grew great as jiedushi of Cai and assumed the imperial title, and was beaten and killed by the combined forces of Zhu Wen and Li Keyong in 888, so that the afterdamp of the revolt ran on for nearly another decade. On the whole, the war closed with the rebel leaders wiped out, the government armies exhausted and the circuits grown strong: the court could no longer organise in Henan or Guanzhong any force that would obey the centre, and the circuits led by Zhu Wen and Li Keyong, having cleaned up the disorder, turned to attacking one another and wore out the last of the Tang's power. In 907 Zhu Wen forced Xizong to abdicate and the Tang dynasty perished, directly linked to the fiscal, military and political structure this war had broken apart.
